# Dora

## Overview

- **Age:** seven years old  <sub>[v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c8 P5](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Dora is a fair child with long, sleek curls that never get out of order, mild hazel eyes, and a straight nose. She has a 'prunes and prisms' mouth and chubby fingers. She often appears neat and proper, dressed in a nicely starched white dress with a black sash.

_Sources: [v2 c8 P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 c8 P25](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0025), [v2 c8 P44](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0044), [v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012)_

## Personality

Dora is extraordinarily good, quiet, demure, and well-behaved, behaving like a model child and a little lady. She is neat, faithful, observant, and industrious, taking great pleasure in helping with small domestic duties and carefully following instructions. However, her temperament is so prim, dispassionate, composed, and monotonous that others sometimes compare her to a book where every page is the same.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c7 P30](../source/v02-c07.md#nw-v02-c07-p0030), [v2 c8 P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 c8 P12](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0012), [v2 c8 P44](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0044), [v2 c10 P85](../source/v02-c10.md#nw-v02-c10-p0085), [v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012), [v2 c24 P10](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0010), [v2 c24 P25](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0025), [v2 c26 P32](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0032), [v2 c26 P33](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0033)_

## History

Dora spent her earliest years under the care of Mary Keith, whose long illness left Dora and her twin brother Davy largely without bringing up. After Mary Keith passed away, Marilla Cuthbert brought Dora and Davy to live with her at Green Gables. At Green Gables, Dora quickly gained a reputation for being an exceptionally well-behaved, quiet, and reliable child who spent her time assisting Marilla with domestic duties and maintaining immaculate clothes and garden plots. She began attending school alongside Davy and made friends, though she once got so frightened by ghost stories told by Mirabel Cotton that she cried and refused to go upstairs alone in the dark. During a fierce and destructive hailstorm at Green Gables, Dora remained calm and quiet by Anne's side throughout the ordeal.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P33](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0033), [v2 c8 P1](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0001), [v2 c16 P12](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0012), [v2 c21 P2](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0002), [v2 c21 P3](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0003), [v2 c21 P7](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0007), [v2 c24 P10](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0010), [v2 c24 P24](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0024), [v2 c24 P25](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0025)_
